question: Can joint nonlinear interactions recover some errors on which every current member agrees? The earlier trees mainly saw generic text shape; adding a different representational head is a distinct direction from reweighting the four existing answers.
method: Among seven previously fitted audition candidates, use the 1319 nomination rows to choose the two highest-accuracy distinct frozen backbones with a supported standalone embedding provider. The algorithm takes their actual discovered identities. On the original 2685 fitting rows only, center and scale each encoder's per-text coordinates and fit 16 label-blind principal directions. Each text receives both reduced representations and the ordinary language-agnostic shape statistics already provided by the codebase. Use signed option difference and symmetric pair midpoint. Fit one histogram gradient-boosting classifier with 120 iterations, 7 leaves, learning rate .06, min leaf size max(12,ceil(sqrt(n)/2)), L2=1, no early stopping; train both option orders and complement probabilities at inference. No list of favored words, data names, row identities or examples of persistent errors is used in construction or training.
evaluation: On the 1318 confirmation rows choose 0,25,50 or 100% for the new prediction against the already frozen four-member portfolio, always preferring its zero share on ties. Report how many of the errors all four members made are corrected by the standalone head and how many previously correct votes a blend loses. If the best share is positive, freeze it and score 1309 separate audit rows. Require strictly positive gains on both panels and >=+0.20 percentage points pooled before a larger candidate study. The fitting and scoring panels are all group-disjoint within this study but reused for software development in earlier trials. A research fit is not an independent ordinary-agent course result.
usage: One new local supervised classifier fit, two unsupervised projections. Reuse previously fitted classifiers for the selection and baseline. No model API or designated validation, test or H2.
